story: Hi doctor, so it started less than two days ago. I've had no appetite at all, and I've been feeling sick to my stomach — I actually threw up a few times. The weird thing is, the vomiting always came after the belly pain started, not before.
At first the pain was around my belly button, kind of up in the middle area. Then it moved down to the lower right side. And it's gotten worse over time — it's really starting to bother me now.
When it hurts, I just want to lie down, curl up with my knees pulled up toward my chest, and not move, because moving around makes the pain worse.
I haven't had any diarrhea or constipation — nothing like that. And I don't have a fever.
Hi doctor. So over the past six months or so, I've had this pain in my upper right belly — it's happened three times now, and the last time was about two weeks ago.

All three episodes were pretty much the same. The last one started as a kind of dull, constant discomfort in the upper right part of my belly. It was mild at first, but it quickly turned into a steady pain — not crampy or colicky, just constant. It lasted about five hours, and then it gradually eased off. I do remember the pain spreading to my back and my chest. I felt like I might have had a bit of a fever, but I didn't have any chills. I didn't notice any yellowing of my skin or eyes, and I only threw up once.
I haven't really noticed any connection between the pain and eating or any particular food. And changing position or moving around doesn't seem to make it better or worse either.

I've had a bit of a sensitive stomach in the past — things like cabbage, okra, and beets tend to bother me, but that's always just been bloating and gas, never actual pain. I haven't tried eating those again recently. I've also been avoiding greasy, fried, and spicy foods, though I can't really say exactly why.
I've never had heartburn, reflux, or a burning feeling in my upper belly. No weight loss, no change in my bowel habits, and no black stools.

Hi doctor. So I've had this cough for about four days now. At first it was dry, but then I started coughing up this rusty-colored phlegm. Then last night, all of a sudden, I got the chills and felt feverish and just generally awful — achy, rundown, the works. At first I figured it was just a cold, but it's been getting worse instead of better. I barely slept last night because I was coughing so much.

I don't feel short of breath exactly, but I think I might be breathing a little faster than usual. And on the way here, after one long coughing fit, I got this sharp pain in the right side of my chest. I haven't had any swelling in my legs, and it doesn't get worse when I lie flat. No pain on the left side or in the middle of my chest. And no stomach issues — no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
As for my history, I have high blood pressure and high cholesterol. I haven't taken any antibiotics in the past three months.
notes: Note: the physical exam findings (fever 101.3°F, HR 102, RR 24, SpO₂ 94%, dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds at the right lower lung base)

story: Hi doctor. So I've been having trouble breathing, a cough, some wheezing, and chest tightness for a few years now. In the beginning, it came and went — mostly in the winter — and I'd be totally fine in between. But over the last few years, it's been there pretty much all the time, and every now and then it gets worse. The breathing is worse at night, and sometimes during the day too. Cold air, dust, and any kind of activity make it worse. I don't have to prop myself up to breathe at night, and I don't wake up gasping — nothing like that.

The cough is usually dry, though sometimes I bring up a little bit of phlegm. No blood. I cough both day and night, and it's worse when I'm around dust or cold air. The wheezing and chest tightness come along with the cough. In fact, I've been hospitalized twice in the last two months because the breathing and coughing got so bad.

Now that you mention it, I do sometimes get a runny nose and sneezing, especially around dust. No chest pain, no weight loss, no fever. My bowels and urination are normal. Nothing that points to a heart problem or reflux that I know of. My brother has asthma and food allergies.

As for my habits, I've smoked about 10 to 15 cigarettes a day for the past 10 years. I've never worked around cotton or coal dust. Right now I'm on a bronchodilator and a steroid inhaler, and in the past I've taken theophylline, ketotifen, and montelukast.
notes: Note: the exam findings — the upright/propped-up posture, nasal polyps on exam, pulse 120, BP 120/70, RR 24, and the negative findings on general exam

story: Hi doctor. So I've been getting these high fevers recently. They come and go — I'll get chills and shivering with them. I tried some over-the-counter antibiotics on my own, but they didn't help at all.
I've noticed the fever tends to get worse in the evening, and it seems to hit every other day. When it comes on, I feel just awful — rundown, no appetite, and kind of nauseous.
notes: Note: the exam findings — appearing thin, weak, pale, and having an enlarged spleen

story: Doctor, I've been putting on weight and my whole body has been swelling up — it's been going on for a few months now, and it keeps getting worse. The odd thing is, I'm barely eating anything; my appetite is gone. I've been feeling really tired and weak, and achy all over. I can't stand the cold — I always want to be somewhere warm. I've been constipated, and I feel sleepy most of the time, even when I'm supposed to be working. My concentration and memory have gone downhill since this all started. My voice has changed too — it's gone hoarse recently. And my skin feels rough and dry.

I haven't had any chest pain, palpitations, or trouble breathing. No tingling or numbness in my hands or feet, and I haven't passed out. My periods have been very heavy for the last few months — they used to be normal. I don't have high blood pressure or diabetes. No history of thyroid problems, thyroid surgery, or radiation to the neck. I haven't given birth or had a difficult delivery in the last six months. I wasn't on any medications, including birth control pills, before this started. No one else in my family has had anything like this. I was given calcium tablets and vitamins at some point.
notes: Note: "a few months" blurs 2–3 months; "at some point" blurs the calcium/vitamin timing; the source only denies childbirth in the last 6 months, so no fuller obstetric history is implied.

story: Doctor, I've had this discomfort in my upper stomach for about two years now. It's there every day — it comes and goes in how bad it is, but it never really goes away. Eating tends to make it worse. And I feel really full, even after a normal-sized meal, nothing big. My weight hasn't changed. My only other medical thing is the occasional migraine. I had my appendix out as a kid and my wisdom teeth out when I was a teenager. I don't smoke, and I hardly ever drink. Nothing runs in the family that I know of.

I've had a bunch of tests done over the past couple of years — an upper GI series, an ultrasound and a HIDA scan, an endoscopy, and some kind of gastric emptying scan — and I was told they all came back normal. I really just want to know what this is and what can be done about it.
notes: Note: tests are blurred into "a bunch of tests" without exact intervals; H. pylori and lab results are omitted because the source marks them as not necessarily known to the patient; ages are blurred to "as a kid" / "when I was a teenager.

story: Doctor, I woke up yesterday morning with this rash on both my arms and wrists. It's really itchy. It's been getting worse since it appeared. It got more irritated after I showered. I tried some Benadryl cream on it, but it didn't help. I don't have any medical history otherwise.
notes: Note: rash morphology (red papules, excoriations) is examination findings and is omitted; absence of web-space lesions/burrows is examination and omitted; clinician uncertainty and the permethrin/dermatology referral are visit management, not pre-visit history, and omitted; "yesterday morning" blurs "1 day prior.

story: Doctor, for the past two days it's been burning when I pee — it comes and goes. I've also been going more often and feeling like I have to go urgently. Once, I saw blood in my urine. I don't have a fever and my back doesn't hurt. I tried cranberry juice and some Pyridium 200 mg I had left over from a previous urinary infection. My urine looks dark now. I've had two urinary infections in the past year — the last one was a few months ago — and both cleared up with antibiotics I was given. I've never had a kidney infection.

I've been sexually active since I was 18. I'm on the pill and I haven't missed any. I'm in a monogamous relationship right now and I believe my partner is too. I've only ever had one sexual partner. No history of any sexually transmitted infections. My last period was three weeks ago, right on time. I don't have any children.
notes: Note: antibiotic name/dose/duration blurred to "antibiotics I was given"; "a few months ago" blurs 4 months; exam findings (afebrile, no suprapubic or CVA tenderness) omitted; pregnancy status is not established — the source only says no missed pills.

story: Doctor, I was in a car crash — the weather was bad — on my way home from dinner with friends. My seatbelt and the airbag saved my life. Since then I've been struggling with fatigue and headaches, and my memory is poor. This is shortly after I got out of the hospital.

My wife is here with me — she can tell you more about how I've been at home. She says my language seems okay, but I have trouble finishing anything I start, I forget what she told me a few minutes before, and I get confused easily all of a sudden. She wonders if the crash caused all this.
notes: Note: exact time since injury is unspecified in the source and is left vague; "mild-to-moderate head injury" is a clinician assessment and is not put in the patient's mouth; cognitive test results are assessment results and omitted; wife-reported items are explicitly attributed to her to preserve the collateral source.

story: I’m 68, and I had a heart attack six months ago. They put a stent in one of the arteries in my heart. Lately I’ve been feeling tired and having trouble sleeping. I wake up at night short of breath, and I sleep better if I use pillows to prop up my head and chest. I still do the same exercises I started after my heart attack, but they leave me more and more out of breath.
I’m 38, and I’ve been having pain low down in my belly. It gets really bad during my period. My periods are heavy, and sometimes I bleed in between them, too. I’m married and have three children.

I’m 22 and seven months pregnant. Heat really bothers me, and I can feel my heart pounding. I feel completely worn out, and I get short of breath when I do things that take some effort. I’ve also noticed a couple of changes in how I look. My eyes have been sticking out more for about six months, and several months ago I noticed patches on my legs.

My mother is 77. She was cooking in the kitchen when she collapsed onto the floor, and I called an ambulance. She slowly regained consciousness over the next two days. When she woke up, she couldn’t move the right side of her face or her right arm. She couldn’t feel it when those areas were touched, either. She understood what we said to her, but she couldn’t answer our questions out loud. It was easier for her to write down what she wanted to say.
notes: Note: Her daughter is describing the episode after her mother regained consciousness. The patient can also communicate in writing.

story: I’m 31. For four days I’ve felt really sick to my stomach and have been throwing up. I can’t even keep drinks down. I’ve felt tired and weak for about a week, and I get a little short of breath when I’m active. Two days ago I noticed swelling in my lower legs, face, and arms. I’m only passing a little urine, and it looks brown, but it doesn’t hurt when I pee. About two weeks ago I had a really sore throat and felt feverish. Both went away after a few days. I don’t have a fever or chills now, and I haven’t had a cough, belly pain, diarrhea, or constipation.

My daughter is six days old. For about six hours she’s been fussier than usual and hasn’t been feeding as much. Her temperature was 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit. She was born vaginally at 39 weeks. My pregnancy went smoothly, and I had my regular prenatal checkups. I didn’t have any illnesses or infections during the pregnancy, and the only thing I took was a prenatal vitamin.
notes: Note: The mother provides the history. The pregnancy details and prenatal vitamin use refer to her.

story: I’m 65, and I’ve been getting more short of breath over the last five years. This past year I’ve also had trouble coughing up phlegm. Usually only a little comes up, and it’s clear. This past week the amount has changed, and now I’m bringing up yellow phlegm throughout the day. My breathing has gotten worse this week, too. I feel short of breath even when I’m sitting still. I used to work as a garage mechanic. I don’t know of anything I was exposed to at work, and I’ve never had asthma, breathing problems as a child, or allergies.

I’m 38. For two or three months I’ve had a low fever on and off. Sometimes it goes up in the evening, and I sweat at night, but I don’t get chills or start shaking. I have a dry cough that’s worse at night, and I get short of breath when I exert myself. I’ve been feeling really weak. Over the past three months I’ve lost a lot of weight and haven’t had much appetite. A few days ago I noticed lumps on the right side of my neck, then under my arms and in my groin. They don’t hurt, but they’re getting bigger.

I’m 19. Three days after I came home from college for spring break, I got a fever and a headache and noticed a rash on my body. Then I felt sick to my stomach, threw up, and found that the light really bothered me. After that, tiny spots appeared on my arms and legs. Within a few hours, those spots had spread to my body, too. I don’t have any known medicine allergies, and I don’t know of any contact with ticks.
notes: Note: This paragraph is the patient’s account of her symptoms. The source also records that she became agitated and combative on the way to the hospital. That detail belongs in an observer’s account.

story: I’m 67. My upper partial denture bothers me, and the teeth on the top right hurt. My mouth feels dry, and I see a little blood when I brush. I haven’t seen a dentist in three years. I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes eight years ago. My feet feel strange when I walk, almost like I’m walking on clouds. I also broke my wrist recently without much of an injury. The bone doctor recommended a bone density test, but I haven’t had it yet.

I’m 44. Around half past midnight, while I was asleep, I got really intense pain right behind my breastbone. It lasted a long time and stayed in my chest without spreading anywhere else. I broke out in a heavy cold sweat with the pain. I have high blood pressure, and I’ve been told my cholesterol and blood fat levels are abnormal.

I’m 28. I’ve had white vaginal discharge on and off for seven or eight months, and it smells bad. I have to pee often, and it burns when I go. My periods are heavy and painful. I also have pain low down in my belly and an ache in my back. The pain makes it hard to get my usual chores done.

I’m 18. About two years ago I suddenly started feeling thirsty all the time and peeing a lot, and it’s been like that ever since. I drink about seven or eight quarts of water a day, and I really prefer it ice-cold. I get up three or four times every night to pee. Apart from that, I generally feel okay, though my voice is high-pitched and lately my vision has been a little blurry.

My son is four. For the last two days he’s had a runny nose and a cough that brings up phlegm. I can hear him wheezing, too. Today he felt hot and didn’t want to eat as much as usual. As far as I know, he’s never had any heart or lung problems, and he’s up to date on his shots. His two younger siblings are both getting over chest colds.
notes: Note: The parent reports that the child felt hot. The recorded temperature of 103.2°F was measured during the clinic exam.

story: I’m 52, and I’ve had bouts of coughing for several years where I bring up a lot of mucus. At first it only happened in winter and lasted two or three months. For the past month I’ve been coughing day and night. It’s worse in the morning, and cold air or dust makes me cough more. Sometimes my whole chest feels tight, especially when I cough. I get short of breath when I do something that takes a fair bit of effort, and resting helps. Two years ago the coughing and breathlessness got so bad that I had to stay in the hospital. I smoke. I haven’t coughed up blood or had chest pain, fever, swollen ankles, or weight loss.

I’m 40, and I’ve been feeling very weak for two or three months. It’s gradually getting worse, and now even my usual daily activities are hard to do. For about three months I’ve sometimes felt dizzy or light-headed. Both my feet tingle and feel numb, and I sometimes get cramps in my calves. Over those same three months, I’ve felt my heart pounding, lost my appetite, and lost weight. I haven’t noticed any unusual bleeding, and my periods haven’t been heavy. I haven’t had a fever, trouble swallowing, or any changes in my bowel or bladder habits. I’ve been given iron tablets, multivitamins, and ranitidine.

I’m 44. I had my right wisdom tooth pulled, and five days later the area under my chin started swelling. It keeps getting bigger. It hurts, and I’m having trouble opening my mouth and swallowing. I’ve had a fever and chills. It’s also hard to breathe, especially when I lie back. I don’t have any known allergies to medicines.

I’m 57, and I’ve had irritable bowel syndrome for 20 years, with constipation as my main problem. It used to be well controlled with Lexapro 20 mg a day and occasional milk of magnesia. When I traveled to Asia nine months ago, I went several days without a bowel movement. Then, for a few days, my stools were hard, like little pebbles, and difficult to pass. Now I go two or three times a day, but I have to push really hard and never feel like I’ve emptied my bowels completely. I don’t see any blood, and it doesn’t hurt when I go. I tried adding fiber, but it made my belly feel uncomfortably bloated. This has been disruptive enough that I miss two or three days of work each month, and sometimes I miss social plans, too.

I’m 37. Two days ago I suddenly started having pain in the skin between my little toe and the toe next to it on my left foot. It hurts so much that even putting my shoe on is difficult. I tried some over-the-counter Lotrimin for athlete’s foot, but it didn’t help. The nails on those same two toes have been thick and yellow for years. The pain is new.

I’m 52. I felt fine yesterday and went to a crab feast that afternoon. Then last night I woke up with terrible pain in my right knee. It was swollen and warm, and I hadn’t injured it. I’ve felt feverish and sweaty, but I haven’t checked my temperature. None of my other joints hurt right now. Several years ago I had really bad pain in my left big toe, and it got better when I took aspirin. I also have high blood pressure and take hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
